note: The three-rule index behind every chapter's recall slide: ten laws, three buckets, one page.

buckets.title: What is true
buckets.summary: Four laws about state: when a record exists, where its numbers live, and why a balanced book can still be wrong.

buckets.title: Where it lives
buckets.summary: Three laws about structure: hierarchies, ownership of a field, and the order defaults resolve in.

buckets.title: How it moves
buckets.summary: Three laws about action: one document per event, who may do or see what, and the close that ends a period.

laws.law: Nothing exists until it is submitted.
laws.detail: A draft writes no ledger row, no stock row and no number in the series. Treat drafts as unfinished work, not as records.

laws.law: Quantity lives in the stock ledger, value in the general ledger, and one voucher writes both.
laws.detail: Every receipt, delivery or stock entry creates stock ledger entries and, at the same moment, the GL rows that carry their value.
Double entry proves that debits equal credits, not that they landed in the right accounts. Only a report or a reconciliation proves correctness.

laws.law: History is append-only: cancel and amend, never edit.
laws.detail: Submitted documents are evidence. The correction path is a reversal, a credit note or an amendment that keeps the original visible.

laws.law: Masters go broad to narrow: company, then group, then item or party.
laws.detail: Item groups, territories, cost centres and account trees are hierarchies that reports roll up. A flat list works only until the first report.

laws.law: Greyed out means a setting upstream owns the field.
laws.detail: Batch fields appear when Has Batch No is on, tax fields when a template exists. A disabled field is a message about configuration, not a bug.

laws.law: Defaults cascade: global, company, party or item, then the transaction.
laws.detail: Each level may override the one above, which is why one wrong customer price list can look like a broken pricing rule.

laws.law: Exactly one document owns each event; skipping it leaves a permanent trace.
laws.detail: Skipping the receipt leaves interim stock uncleared, skipping the delivery leaves the order open. No shortcut leaves no trace.

laws.law: Roles decide what you can do; user permissions decide what you can see.
laws.detail: A role grants actions on a DocType, a user permission filters the rows. When a report looks wrong, check both before changing either.

laws.law: Close the period; do not edit the past.
laws.detail: The Period Closing Voucher posts the closing entries and locks the period, so later corrections belong to the current period with a note.
